title: Power Pages: client APIs for scripting forms, lists, users and data
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, documented APIs, permission boundaries, licensing requirements and configuration routes are supported. It preserves the roadmap's conflicting release-phase labels and correctly distinguishes an undocumented client-API switch from the documented Web API table controls.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Developers use the new APIs by adding calls to site scripts rather than through an automatic change to visitor-facing UI.
claims.quote: Each example is complete, so you can copy it into a JavaScript web file or into the **Custom JavaScript** section of a page, and then change the form names, column names, and table names to match your site.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Risk assessment; controls[0].note; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Power Pages enforces table permissions on the server and the client API cannot override them.
claims.quote: Power Pages applies form metadata and table permissions on the server, and the client API can't override those settings.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Web roles associated with table permissions determine the record access available to Web API callers.
claims.quote: The portal Web API accesses table (entity) records and follows the table permissions given to users through the associated web role.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Granting the Anonymous users web role table access makes the table's data accessible to visitors, subject to the stated tenant restriction.
claims.quote: When the Anonymous users web role is granted access to a table, any user who visits the site can access the data in the table.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The tenant Anonymous access to Dataverse control can override maker table permissions and prevent anonymous reads.
claims.quote: Selecting **All sites** blocks anonymous access in all the websites in the tenant, overriding any maker configurations that provide access to anonymous users.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Blocking anonymous viewing with the tenant control does not prevent unauthenticated users from writing Dataverse data.
claims.quote: While unauthenticated users will be prevented from viewing Dataverse data when this setting is enabled, these users can still write data to Dataverse.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: setVisible(false) only hides a control in the browser; Microsoft advises using table permissions and column security to protect data.
claims.quote: The `setVisible(false)` method hides a control in the browser only. Use table permissions and column security to protect data. Never rely on hiding a control to secure data.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: row.setVisible(false) changes the list presentation, not the underlying data or server-returned record count.
claims.quote: Hiding a row changes only what people see in the list; it doesn't change the data or the number of records that the server returns.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Client-side setDisabled changes do not override server-enforced restrictions.
claims.quote: When a control is locked on the server, such as a multiselect picklist on a read-only form or field, the `setDisabled(false)` method has no effect.
